Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 45-year-old woman with 3–4 months of painful, itchy, fissured palmar dryness following increased occupational exposure to cleaning agents and infrequent glove use.  
• Type 2 diabetes (current therapy: metformin).  

Working diagnosis  
• Irritant contact dermatitis of the hands – high likelihood given direct temporal relationship with new housekeeping job, unprotected chemical exposure, palmar localization, pain > itch.

Differential considerations  
• Allergic contact dermatitis to cleaning products – medium likelihood; consider patch testing if no improvement.  
• Chronic hand (atopic) eczema – low likelihood due to lack of atopic history and clear occupational trigger.

Management  
• Avoid triggers: strict glove use when using cleaning products.  
• Pharmacologic: Prescribed topical corticosteroid cream (strength not documented) + stronger emollient; apply 3–4 times/day for 10–14 days.  
• Review: Return in 1–2 weeks, or sooner if spread or worsening.  
• Contingency: If persistent, consider alternative therapies and/or dermatology referral.

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  
  • Advised on skin protection, moisturization, and trigger avoidance.  
  • No specific diabetes self-management or lifestyle counseling documented.

- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Review in 10–14 days; earlier if deterioration.

- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Dermatology referral if no response to current therapy (not yet actioned).  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not recorded

- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Irritant contact dermatitis – High likelihood: Temporal link to unprotected chemical exposure; palmar distribution; pain and fissures predominate.  
2. Allergic contact dermatitis – Medium likelihood: Occupational exposure to multiple potential allergens; intermittent itch; possible sensitization.  
3. Chronic hand (atopic) eczema – Low likelihood: Chronic fissured eczema fits but no atopic history and clear occupational trigger present.
